chunks: And it is narrated from Ya‘qūb ibn Shu‘ayb, who said:
I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام about fasting on the Day of ‘Arafah. He said: “If you wish, you may fast, and if you wish, you may refrain from fasting.”

And he mentioned: “A man came to al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام and found one of them fasting and the other breaking the fast. So he asked them, and they said: ‘If you fast, it is good; and if you do not fast, it is permissible.’”

key_terms.لَمْ تَصُمْ: you did not fast / you do not fast

ai.seo_question: Is fasting on the Day of ‘Arafah obligatory or optional in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith indicates that fasting on the Day of ‘Arafah is optional, not obligatory. The statement of al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام further confirms that both fasting and leaving it are acceptable, though fasting is described as good.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1809 - It is narrated from Ya‘qub ibn Shu‘ayb, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)) about fasting on the Day of Arafah.
Imam (as) said: 'If you wish, you may fast, and if you wish, you may refrain from fasting.'
Imam (as) mentioned: 'A man came to al-Hasan (as) and al-Husayn (as) and found one of them fasting and the other not fasting. He asked them, and they said: "If you fast, it is good, and if you do not fast, it is permissible."’"
